correctness.rationale: The complete first rectangular Fourier band forces E[e_d(p)]=2^-d and E[e_(d−1)(p)]=d2^-(d−1) for p_j=cos² π(x_j−a_j). If support avoids a sup cube of radius R, at least one p_j≤s=cos²πR; pointwise e_(d−1)≥(s^-1+d−1)e_d, including zero-coordinate boundaries. Integrating yields s≥1/(d+1) and sharp r_d. For each d, replacing the d+1 missing half-period cube vertices by 2d contact points with weights (d+1)/(d2^(d+1)) preserves every first-band Fourier character by a direct count in support size. Equality in the nonnegative deficit forces only contact points or ≥2 antipodal-coordinate skeleton; the e_d and e_(d−1) moments fix contact weights and sine moments split ± masses. A four-atom displacement along the skeleton keeps moments and hole for d≥3, proving nonuniqueness. Independently evaluated all 3^d characters for d=2,3,4,5 with errors ≤5.6e-16; dimension-general proof is the symmetric-polynomial argument.
